page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 20 vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 4.8 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15656.89 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9947.0. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a notable strength, placing in the top 25% with a throughput of 185.99 GB/sec. However, the shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core testing falling into the bottom 10%. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 2056.95 GB/sec, large-block uncached write bandwidth is weak at 21.6 GB/sec.

This server type offers high resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that can leverage multiple cores without requiring continuous dedicated CPU performance. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, Redis caching, and static web serving. It is less suitable for single-threaded applications, memory-write intensive tasks, or complex LLM text generation due to the shared CPU model and poor single-core performance.
